defects.description: The total adds decimal-dollar values as binary floating-point numbers, so repeated one-cent rows make the grand total drift from the exact integer-cent sum.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { makeRows, total } from "./src/total.js"; const rows = makeRows(10_000); console.log(JSON.stringify({ rows: rows.length, total: total(rows) }));'

defects.why_missed: The happy suite sums only a few exactly representable amounts, so repeated one-cent additions never reach the scale that exposes binary drift.

defects.description: parseFloat stops at the comma in a grouped amount, so 1,234.56 is counted as 1 instead of 1,234.56.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { total } from "./src/total.js"; console.log(JSON.stringify({ input: "1,234.56", total: total([{ amount: "1,234.56" }]) }));'

defects.why_missed: The happy suite uses ungrouped decimal strings and never checks whether a comma-formatted amount contributes its full value.

traps.description: Each row's display value is rounded independently to cents for presentation; the display helper does not alter the aggregate.
